declared.title: Decisions and revisions: The affective forecasting of changeable outcomes
declared.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
declared.foundIn: nommée dans la consigne de la session ; titre relevé sur la recherche Crossref « decisions and revisions affective forecasting of changeable outcomes » du 2026-11-22 : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: photography students (study 1) and other participants (studies 2a, 2b); US; sample sizes not given in the abstract

findings.text: Students who could still change their mind about which print to keep liked it less than students whose choice was final

support.sentence: However, those who had the opportunity to change their minds liked their prints less than those who did not (Study 1).

findings.text: Being able to change one's mind weakened the processes that usually make people like what they chose, yet most participants wanted that option

support.sentence: Although the opportunity to change their minds impaired the postdecisional processes that normally promote satisfaction (Study 2a), most participants wanted to have that opportunity (Study 2b).

limits: small laboratory studies on a choice of little importance (a photo print)
no direct replication found (OpenAlex citing works and Europe PMC, 2026-11-22; same in the counter-evidence report)
